answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each identity must answer unpredictable cross-agent queries linking its recent actions to a shared reference point, like a bridge between two signed checkpoints. Clones share one history, so they cannot produce divergent answers under separate challenge keys. At least one of N clones always fails, exposing the cluster at a measured delta in error rates. An attacker must run distinct decision paths per identity, costing a full juniper-sized compute budget for every clone kept live.
